title: Optimization and Refinement of Anti-Infective Therapy for Spondylodiscitis: A Retrospective Single-Center Study
summary:
Spondylodiscitis is a rare infection of the spine. In recent decades, this disease has been diagnosed more frequently. The diagnosis is often difficult because the symptoms are nonspecific and many affected patients already have several other medical conditions. In addition, the causative pathogen can only be clearly identified in about half to two-thirds of cases.

In this study, patient data from a hospital will be analyzed retrospectively in order to improve antibiotic treatment. Two main questions will be investigated:
1) Can the analysis of existing antibiotic susceptibility tests help provide better treatment recommendations when no pathogen has been identified?
2) Can clinical findings and laboratory values be used to identify groups of patients who have a particularly high risk of a severe disease course?

The statistical analysis will mainly serve to generate new hypotheses. In total, data from about 500 patients will be analyzed. This number should be sufficient to examine common pathogens and their combinations and to estimate how frequently they occur.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all adult patients diagnosed with spondylodiscitis who were treated at Unfallkrankenhaus Berlin between 2010 and 2025, irrespective of the primary treating department.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All adult patients with spondylodiscitis treated between 2010 and 2025, irrespective of the primary treating department.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients younger than 18 years at the time of treatment
